hints: Focus on which carbon atoms in but-2-ene are sp3 and which are sp2, since only sp3 carbons contribute here.
Notice that but-2-ene, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH=CHCH}_3$, has two $\text{CH}_3$ carbons that are sp3 and two $\text{CH}$ carbons that are sp2.
Count how many sigma bonds each sp3 carbon forms, remembering each bond uses one sp3 orbital from that carbon.
walkthrough:
**Draw the structure and label hybridisation**

Think of but-2-ene as $\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}=\text{CH}-\text{CH}_3$. Lovely and symmetrical.

Carbons 1 and 4 have four single-bond regions, so they are $sp^3$. Carbons 2 and 3 have a double bond, so they are $sp^2$.

**Recall what an sp3 carbon uses**

An $sp^3$ carbon has four $sp^3$ hybrid orbitals. Each one overlaps to make one sigma bond.

Rule to remember:
$$\text{number of } sp^3 \text{ orbitals used} = \text{number of sigma bonds from } sp^3 \text{ atoms}$$

**Count bonds from the two sp3 carbons**

Each $\text{CH}_3$ carbon forms 3 $\text{C-H}$ bonds plus 1 $\text{C-C}$ bond. That is 4 sigma bonds, so 4 $sp^3$ orbitals used per carbon.

Calculation:
$$2 \times 4 = 8$$

**Check nothing else counts**

The $sp^2$ carbons use $sp^2$ orbitals, not $sp^3$, and H uses $1s$. The unhybridised $p$ orbitals in the pi bond also do not count. So the total stays at 8.

options.A: 2 is far too low. It might come from counting only the two C-C sigma bonds from the sp3 carbons and forgetting the six C-H bonds they also form.
options.B: 4 is the number for one methyl carbon only. It misses that but-2-ene has two CH3 groups, so you must double it.
options.C: 6 counts only the six C-H bonds from the two CH3 groups. It forgets the two C-C sigma bonds (CH3-CH) which also use one sp3 orbital each.
options.D: 8 is correct. The two sp3 carbons each use all four of their sp3 orbitals: 3 for C-H and 1 for C-C, giving 2 x 4 = 8 orbitals used in sigma bonding.
